summary: @servicetitan/modularpayments-webfields preinstall downloads Bun and executes obfuscated payload
details: Package declares preinstall `node setup.mjs`. setup.mjs is a hex-obfuscated script that, when `bun` is absent from PATH, downloads a Bun runtime binary from `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v<version>/<arch>.zip`, unzips it to a temp directory, chmods 0o755, and invokes it via `execFileSync` against a shipped sibling `math_init.js` — a 727KB `// @bun @bun-cjs` bundle with rotated-string-array obfuscation and a custom decoder function (`hc1jfK9`), not human-readable and not analyzable without executing under Bun. This is the alternate-runtime dropper pattern: on `npm install`, an opaque obfuscated payload executes under a freshly fetched non-Node runtime, bypassing Node-focused inspection. The package presents itself as ServiceTitan's payments webfields SDK (author `Payments Squad @ ServiceTitan`, `index.ts` referencing `stpaymentspciprod.blob.core.windows.net/webfields/1.0.52/webfields.js`), but a payment-types SDK has no legitimate reason to ship an obfuscated Bun-runtime dropper at preinstall — indicating publisher compromise or impersonation.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
